standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness of the image of a quasi-compact open, and the existence of a quasi-compact open containing it
standard_prerequisites.use: For a quasi-compact open $U \subset X$ it produces a quasi-compact open $V \subset Y$ containing $f(U)$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local finiteness of a family of closed subsets tested on quasi-compact opens
standard_prerequisites.use: Only finitely many $Z_i$ meet the quasi-compact open $V$, and the inclusion of index sets transfers that finiteness to the preimages meeting $U$.

core_obligations: Fix a quasi-compact open subset $U \subset X$ (proof line 2181).
Choose a quasi-compact open $V \subset Y$ containing the image $f(U)$, using quasi-compactness of that image (proof lines 2182-2184).
Compare the index sets: those $i$ with $f^{-1}(Z_i) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ form a subset of those with $Z_i \cap V \neq \emptyset$, which is finite by assumption (proof lines 2185-2190).
proof_roadmap: Choice of a quasi-compact open in the source (proof line 2181).
A quasi-compact open in the target containing its image (proof lines 2182-2184).
Inclusion of index sets gives finiteness (proof lines 2185-2190).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pulling back a locally finite family of closed subsets along an arbitrary morphism between schemes locally of finite type preserves local finiteness (statement lines 2169-2178). The proof tests local finiteness on an arbitrary quasi-compact open of the source, finds a quasi-compact open of the target containing its image, and compares the two index sets. The comparison of index sets through a quasi-compact intermediate is the substance, so the claim is H2.
